(n.un. ة) 1a ben tree (Moringa; bot. ); b hone-radish tree (Moringa oleifera; bot. ); 2 Egyptian willow (Salix aegyptiaca L.; bot. ) – WehrCowan1976 ▪ also ǧawz al-bān ‘nut of bān’, item grouped elsewhere sub ↗√BWN or ↗√BYN. – Of obscure origin, prob. a loanword. The type of tree it indicates varies across the languages in which it is attested, also within the Arabic-speaking area itself. ▪ Vennemann2006 (following Tazi1998) assumes an Ind etymology (Ind behen , cf. also Pers bān ). ▪ … ▪ … ▪ DRS 2 (1994) #BYN-2: Akk bīn , JP Syr bīnā ‘tamarisque’, Ar bān : arbre qui donne la noix muscade; saule d’Egypte; MġrAr bān ‘cassie, arbuste et sa fleur; guilandina morynga; mimosa gumifera’ ▪ … ▪ DRS 2 (1994) ad #BYN-2: Akk > Aram? ; pour l’Aram PayneSmith 519: «tamarisk», commentaire: «willow?». ▪ For Vennemann’s ( ▪ … ▪ Ge Ben (nuss) ‘(nut of) Moringa arabica pers.’, via mLat ben from Ar bān , also ǧawz al-bān ‘nut of bān’, also Pers bān , from Ind behen . The variant Behen(nuß) arose from medieval confusion with another plant, Centaurea behen , Pers/Ar bahmān – Vennemann2006 (following Tazi1998). ▪ … – . Cf. also ↗√BWN and ↗BYN.
